Benchmark sparse Cholesky solver settings on a graph

Source: R/solver_benchmark.R
terradish_solver_benchmark.Rd

Times the linear-system setup and solve used internally by terradish_algorithm for a fixed graph and conductance vector. This is intended as a lightweight hardware-specific diagnostic for choosing direct factorization settings on large rasters.

Usage

terradish_solver_benchmark(
  data,
  conductance = NULL,
  factorization = c("simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll", "supernodal_ll"),
  solve_backend = "matrix",
  n_replicates = 1L,
  perm = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A terradish_graph object.

conductance

Optional numeric conductance vector with one value per graph vertex. Defaults to constant conductance.

factorization

Direct solver factorization modes to compare. Supported values are "simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll", and "supernodal_ll".

solve_backend

Direct-solver RHS solve backend to compare. "matrix" uses Matrix's standard solve() method. The experimental "cholmod_cpp" backend calls Matrix's CHOLMOD C API directly from compiled code after the factorization has been built. The experimental "cholmod_cpp_cached" backend also keeps the CHOLMOD factorization/update state inside a compiled external pointer.

n_replicates

Number of times to repeat each setting.

perm

Should CHOLMOD use a fill-reducing permutation?

Value

A data frame with one row per benchmark replicate and columns for graph size, factorization mode, solve backend, setup time, solve time, and total time.

Details

The benchmark isolates the sparse linear algebra step. It does not run a full likelihood optimization, line search, measurement-model subproblem, or Gaussian smoothing update. Use it to learn whether "simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll", or "supernodal_ll" is fastest on a particular machine and graph size, then pass the preferred choice through solver_control = list(factorization = "...") in terradish when using the direct solver. Use solve_backend to evaluate whether either experimental C++ CHOLMOD path is faster for the right-hand-side count used by the graph. The cached backend is most informative when compared inside a full optimization, where nearby evaluations can reuse the same symbolic analysis.

Very small rasters can give noisy timings because setup and R overhead are a large fraction of elapsed time. The comparison is most informative on graphs large enough that Cholesky factorization is a visible part of the fit time.

See also

terradish_assess_settings, terradish

Other solver settings: print.terradish_setting_assessment(), slim_terradish(), terradish_assess_settings()

Examples

library(terra)
data(melip)
altitude <- terra::unwrap(melip.altitude)
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(altitude) <- "altitude"
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(altitude, terra::crds(coords)))
surface <- conductance_surface(altitude, coords[keep])
# One row per setting: setup (factorization) and solve times in seconds.
terradish_solver_benchmark(
  surface,
  factorization = c("simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll"),
  n_replicates = 1
)
#>   solver  factorization solve_backend replicate n_vertices n_rhs setup_time
#> 1 direct simplicial_ldl        matrix         1      22443    34       0.03
#> 2 direct  simplicial_ll        matrix         1      22443    34       0.05
#>   solve_time total_time
#> 1       0.01       0.08
#> 2       0.01       0.09
